revenue_trend_investigation.question: Is monthly revenue trending up or down, and when did the most significant shift happen?

gold.note: month where the planted Q4-2025 drop begins

task_spec.answer_target: month with the most significant revenue shift

evidence.E1: run_sql: SUM(revenue) by DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date), 24 months
evidence.E2: trend_analysis(order_date, revenue, month, sum): slope -1037.47/month, R2 0.023, p 0.476, Mann-Kendall p 0.337, direction decreasing, not significant, change_point 2025-10-01 mean_shift -60712.17

failed_assertions.message: answer is grouped by 'month' but the question asks for order_date
the summary does not state the primary conclusion '2025-10'

failed_assertions.assertion: _entity_match(answer.primary_entity, gold.entity) and gold entity stated in summary
values: summary has 'October 2025', no ISO date = False
misaligned (from the two agent-side issues above)

revenue_trend_investigation.verdict: evaluator too restrictive, not an analytical mistake
reasons: monthly aggregation of order_date is what the question asks; 'month' is DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)
change point 2025-10-01 equals the gold month; '2025-10' is the same month at month resolution
'October 2025' is the same month written out
the direction answer (slightly decreasing, not significant) is supported by E2; all 9 numeric claims verified
the agent preferred the sustained mean shift (E2) over the single largest month-over-month jump (E3, March 2025), which matches the gold definition
proposed_evaluator_changes_not_applied: treat a time grain derived from the requested date column (month/quarter/week of order_date) as matching that grouping
compare YYYY-MM with YYYY-MM-DD at month resolution
recognise written month names ('October 2025', 'Oct 2025') when checking that the summary states a month
revenue_trend_investigation.user_impact: the same check runs in the product: this run shows as 'completed with issues / misaligned' to a user although the answer is right
